node-1.label: Patient had shortness of breath for 1 month, which worsened over the past 2 days

node-2.label: Patient was a 32-year-old adequately nourished male, worked as a tailor, consumed a mixed diet, had BMI 25.3 kg/m2, and was well-built and nourished; he had no other accompanying symptoms

node-3.label: On examination, he was tachypneic, tachycardic, and had a mild fever; oral thrush was observed and scrapings were sent for fungal culture; SpO2 was 87%; no apparent risk factors for immunosuppressive states were found

node-4.label: Chest X-ray showed scattered inspiratory crackles; chest roentgenogram showed bilateral perihilar infiltrates; blood gas analysis revealed PO2 47 mmHg and PCO2 24 mmHg; HRCT thorax showed ground glass opacities in both lung fields, predominantly perihilar; LDH was elevated at 916 U/L; other routine blood work was normal

node-5.label: High flow oxygen was initiated and he was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit; he remained tachypneic on high flow oxygen and intermittently required noninvasive ventilation; empirical antibiotics, fluconazole, and oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) were started along with steroids

node-6.label: Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Pneumocystis organisms; acid-fast bacteria and routine bacterial and fungal cultures were negative; fungal scrapings grew Candida albicans sensitive to fluconazole; HIV ELISA, Western blot, and HIV-RNA polymerase chain reaction tests were negative

attrs.why: The laboratory expert confirms Pneumocystis pneumonia by BAL showing Pneumocystis organisms with negative bacterial and fungal cultures in a non-HIV host. This corroborates the existing clinical, radiographic, and bronchoscopic evidence, so confidence is slightly raised from 0.96 to 0.98.

The laboratory expert confirms negative bacterial cultures and BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis, further arguing against bacterial pneumonia. With the already low prior probability, confidence is lowered from 0.12 to 0.05.

Ground-glass opacities and hypoxia could suggest interstitial lung disease, but BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis and the overall infectious picture make non-infectious ILD unlikely; both experts concur it is effectively ruled out. Confidence remains low at 0.05.

node-2.label: Patient was a 32-year-old adequately nourished male, worked as a tailor, consumed a mixed diet, had BMI 25.3 kg/m2, and was well-built and nourished; he had no other accompanying symptoms

node-3.label: On examination, he was tachypneic, tachycardic, and had a mild fever; oral thrush was observed and scrapings were sent for fungal culture; SpO2 was 87%; no apparent risk factors for immunosuppressive states were found

node-4.label: Chest X-ray showed scattered inspiratory crackles; chest roentgenogram showed bilateral perihilar infiltrates; blood gas analysis revealed PO2 47 mmHg and PCO2 24 mmHg; HRCT thorax showed ground glass opacities in both lung fields, predominantly perihilar; LDH was elevated at 916 U/L; other routine blood work was normal

node-5.label: High flow oxygen was initiated and he was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit; he remained tachypneic on high flow oxygen and intermittently required noninvasive ventilation; empirical antibiotics, fluconazole, and oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) were started along with steroids

node-6.label: Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Pneumocystis organisms; acid-fast bacteria and routine bacterial and fungal cultures were negative; fungal scrapings grew Candida albicans sensitive to fluconazole; HIV ELISA, Western blot, and HIV-RNA polymerase chain reaction tests were negative

attrs.why: The laboratory expert confirms Pneumocystis pneumonia by BAL showing Pneumocystis organisms with negative bacterial and fungal cultures in a non-HIV host. This corroborates the existing clinical, radiographic, and bronchoscopic evidence, so confidence is slightly raised from 0.96 to 0.98.

The laboratory expert confirms negative bacterial cultures and BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis, further arguing against bacterial pneumonia. With the already low prior probability, confidence is lowered from 0.12 to 0.05.

The laboratory expert confirms negative fungal cultures and BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis, with only oral Candida albicans isolated; invasive fungal pneumonia is therefore very unlikely. Confidence is lowered from 0.08 to 0.04.

Ground-glass opacities and hypoxia could suggest interstitial lung disease, but BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis and the overall infectious picture make non-infectious ILD unlikely; both experts concur it is effectively ruled out. Confidence remains low at 0.05.

node-11.label: Patient was well-nourished (BMI 25.3) with no immunosuppressive risk factors, and HIV ELISA, Western blot and HIV-RNA PCR were all negative, indicating a non-immunocompromised host

attrs.why: The laboratory expert reports repeated CD4 110 cells/µL with inverted CD4:CD8 ratio 0.35 and no HIV/drug risk factors, indicating genuine immunodeficiency rather than an immunocompetent host. This directly contradicts the immunocompetent-host label, so confidence is lowered from 0.30 to 0.10.

node-13.label: Laboratory testing shows a CD4 count of 110 cells/µL with an inverted CD4:CD8 ratio of 0.35

node-14.label: Pneumocystis pneumonia occurring in a non-HIV immunocompromised host with CD4 lymphocytopenia

attrs.why: The laboratory expert confirms PCP by BAL in a non-HIV host and emphasizes repeated CD4 110 cells/µL with inverted CD4:CD8 0.35, establishing a non-HIV immunocompromised host with CD4 lymphocytopenia. The underlying cause remains a separate issue, so confidence is raised from 0.75 to 0.90.

node-15.label: Idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) as the underlying cause

attrs.why: The laboratory expert states idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia remains the leading but unconfirmed cause, supported by repeated CD4 110 cells/µL, inverted CD4:CD8 0.35, and no HIV/drug risk factors. However, exclusion labs are missing, so confidence is raised only from 0.50 to 0.60.

node-16.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to hematologic malignancy (e.g., lymphoma)

attrs.why: The laboratory expert notes malignancy workup is missing, so hematologic malignancy is not excluded as a secondary cause of CD4 lymphocytopenia. However, there remains no lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, or abnormal routine blood work, so confidence remains 0.20.

node-17.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to drug or medication exposure

attrs.why: The laboratory expert specifically reports no drug risk factors, which argues strongly against drug- or medication-induced CD4 lymphocytopenia. Confidence is lowered from 0.10 to 0.05.

node-18.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to an autoimmune or systemic disease

attrs.why: The laboratory expert notes autoimmune workup is missing, so an autoimmune/systemic cause is not formally excluded. No systemic symptoms or serologic findings support it, so confidence remains 0.10.

node-19.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to chronic viral infection (e.g., HTLV-1)

attrs.why: The laboratory expert notes HTLV serology is missing, so a chronic non-HIV viral cause remains unexcluded. No positive viral evidence exists, so confidence is only slightly raised from 0.10 to 0.15.
